claim_verdicts.evidence: Round 2 (carried, section 4 rewording checked). v1.34 Service page, ClusterIP: "Choosing this value makes the Service only reachable from within the cluster. This is the default that is used if you don't explicitly specify a `type` for a Service." ingress.txt lines 2-3: TYPE ClusterIP, EXTERNAL-IP <none>.

Ingress page: "Ingress exposes HTTP and HTTPS routes from outside the cluster to services within the cluster." Ingress rules: "An optional host... A list of paths... each of which has an associated backend defined with a service.name and a service.port.name or service.port.number." Section 3 and summary line 3 now say the host is optional.

v1.34 Ingress page: "Both the host and path must match the content of an incoming request"; "Precise matches require that the HTTP `host` header matches the `host` field." curl filling Host from the URL: RFC 9110 is not a docs root; settled by execution: ingress.txt shows curl to http://ingress.donhang.localhost:18080/... got 200 only once the rule for that host existed. "carries" the name holds (curl also appends :18080).

Carried from round 1. Path types: "Each path in an Ingress is required to have a corresponding path type." Exact: "Matches the URL path exactly and with case sensitivity." Prefix: "Matches based on a URL path prefix split by /... done on a path element by element basis." Examples: Prefix /aaa/bbb vs /aaa/bbbxyz: no match.

Ingress Prerequisites: "You must have an Ingress controller to satisfy an Ingress. Only creating an Ingress resource has no effect." Ingress Controllers (re-fetched round 2): "there must be an ingress controller running. You need to select at least one ingress controller and make sure it is set up in your cluster." Supports "a cluster starts no Ingress controller on its own". The ledger's kube-controller-manager clause was not seen; the lesson does not use it.

Carried from round 1. Traefik Kubernetes Ingress provider reference: the provider "watches for incoming ingresses events" and builds routers, services and handlers from them. Kubernetes Ingress Controllers page: "The Traefik Kubernetes Ingress provider is an ingress controller for the Traefik proxy."

Carried from round 1. Traefik docs do not state the no-match response; execution settles it for this setup: ingress.txt "HTTP 404" before the apply, products and "HTTP 200" after; port 18080 maps only to Traefik's node port 30080 (main.tf lines 18-21, apps/traefik.yaml lines 30-35).

Round 1 suggested_text applied verbatim in section 4; the chart-creates-class wording is gone. Traefik provider reference, ingressClass: "identifies resource objects to be processed". Execution: CLASS traefik, then HTTP 200. Ingress page: "Each Ingress should specify a class, a reference to an IngressClass resource".

Carried from round 1. v1.34 Ingress page: "Ingress controllers frequently use annotations to configure behavior. Review the documentation for your choice of ingress controller to learn which annotations are expected and / or supported." and "In reality, the various Ingress controllers operate slightly differently."

Carried from round 1. Annotations page: "You can use Kubernetes annotations to attach arbitrary non-identifying metadata to objects." "Annotations, like labels, are key/value maps" under metadata.annotations.

Round 1 suggested_text applied ("usually still routes its paths"). Ingress page: "Review the documentation for your choice of ingress controller to learn which annotations are expected and / or supported." and "the various Ingress controllers operate slightly differently", consistent with the hedged wording.

Carried from round 1. tools/extract-code deploy/k8s/lessons/api-ingress.yaml --tag stage-3: line 11 `ingressClassName: traefik`, lines 12-22 rule with host ingress.donhang.localhost, path /api/v1, pathType Prefix, Service api port 8080. File is under deploy/k8s/lessons/, not the config repo.

Claim narrowed to the captured run, as round 1 suggested; section 5 now says "when the script ran, `curl` sent the name `ingress.donhang.localhost` to this machine itself, as the output below shows." ingress.txt: the call to ingress.donhang.localhost:18080 returned products and HTTP 200; no DNS entry for the name exists in the repo.

Round 1: extract-code scripts/k8s/ingress.sh --tag stage-3 lines 8-9, 29, 32, 37 as stated. Round 2 addition: show() read from the submodule working tree (git show not run this round): line 6 `show() { echo "\$ $*"; "$@"; }`, prints `$ <command>` then runs it; lines 8-9 identical to the tag excerpt checked in round 1.

Carried from round 1. Traefik provider reference: it "watches for incoming ingresses events"; throttleDuration: "Minimum amount of time to wait between two Kubernetes events before producing a new configuration." Script line 29 waits up to 60 s for 200; ingress.txt shows 200 after apply.

Repo: apps/traefik.yaml lines 30-37 `type: NodePort`, web nodePort 30080; main.tf lines 18-21 node_port 30080 to host_port 18080 (round 1). New sentence, v1.34 Service page, type: NodePort: "Each node proxies that port (the same port number on every Node) into your Service." "Every node in the cluster configures itself to listen on that assigned port and to forward traffic to one of the ready endpoints associated with that Service."

Round 3, section 5 sentence rewritten: "asks the cloud for an outside IP address that passes what arrives there to the Service". v1.34 Service page, type: LoadBalancer (fetched round 3): "setting the type field to LoadBalancer provisions a load balancer for your Service"; "information about the provisioned balancer is published in the Service's .status.loadBalancer field" (example shows an IP); "Traffic from the external load balancer is directed at the backend Pods."

Round 1 suggested wording applied in sections 4 and 6, the diagram ("forward to a Pod of Service api") and quiz q3.c, q4, q5.c. Ingress rules: backend = service.name and service.port. Traefik provider reference, nativeLBByDefault (default false) allows "Kubernetes Service load balancing between the pods instead of the one provided by Traefik"; by default Traefik picks the Pod itself, found via the Service.

Ingress Prerequisites: "Only creating an Ingress resource has no effect." ingress.txt line 9 "ingress.networking.k8s.io/api created" printed before the rule took effect. kubectl reference, Formatting output (fetched round 2): `-o custom-columns=<spec>` "Print a table using a comma separated list of custom columns." Output shows exactly the named columns NAME CLASS HOST PATH SERVICE.

New claim (round 1 major closed). v1.34 Ingress page: "The Ingress spec has all the information needed to configure a load balancer or proxy server." and "In reality, the various Ingress controllers operate slightly differently." Lesson: "The basic rules are fields Kubernetes itself defines, so other controllers read them too." No claim of identical behaviour. Documents opened round 3: v1.34 Service (type: LoadBalancer); round 2: Ingress, Ingress Controllers, Service, kubectl reference.
